name: PrefEval
ontology_notes: Real public preference-following bench. 1,000 unique preference-query pairs times three forms (explicit, implicit choice-based, implicit persona-driven) equals 3,000 pairs across 20 daily-life topics. Queries are built so a generic answer would violate the preference. Intervening turns are sampled from LMSYS-Chat-1M up to 100k tokens. Tasks are generation (Claude 3 Sonnet judge, four error types) and classification (4-way MCQ). ICLR 2025. Zhao et al. arXiv 2502.09597.

supersession.evidence: Paper studies multiple and conflicting preferences in one conversation and reports that multiple stated preferences improved adherence. That is conflict handling, not a dated overwrite of a biographical fact.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Gap between preference disclosure and query is the difficulty knob (10 turns ~3k tokens up to 300 turns / 100k tokens). No calendar-grounded 'last Tuesday' or months-apart reunion.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One user preference bag versus one chatbot. No character, relationship, or lore types.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: A correct answer must avoid options that violate the preference (example. do not recommend jazz in New Orleans after 'I don't like jazz'). That is preference-constrained generation, not trauma/kink/spoiler silence on a known fact.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Error types are preference-unaware violation, preference hallucination, and related generation failures. Not stored-text jailbreaks of a system persona.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that items. Conflicting preferences are still in-context constraints, not deletions.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Reported number is preference-following accuracy vs turn count. No cost-per-turn meter.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Dataset and scripts are in amazon-science/PrefEval under CC BY-NC 4.0. Generation judging wants Claude 3 Sonnet. Classification can run without an LLM judge. Example scripts use AWS Bedrock.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Would prefer systems that keep a user preference and apply it later without being asked. Useful for companion likes/dislikes. It would not select for character identity, RP, poisoning, forget-that, or cost.

published_eval.name: PrefEval
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper. Zero-shot preference-following accuracy falls below 10% at 10 turns (~3k tokens) for most of 10 evaluated models. README subset (travel-restaurants, explicit, generation). o1-preview 0.50 zero-shot / 0.98 reminder at 10 turns, 0.14 / 0.98 at 300 turns. GPT-4o 0.07 / 0.98 at 10 turns, 0.05 / 0.23 at 300 turns.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether a chatbot infers, retrieves, and proactively follows an explicit or implicit user preference after distractor turns. Generation error types plus MCQ accuracy.
